jamal_mobile: Hey team — hitting consistent mid-stream disconnects when my Android app flips into a corporate VPN (IKEv2). Stream starts fine, then ~40s later client logs ECONNRESET and we see partial output only. Repro steps below.

alex_support: Thanks, can you paste the client logs + the request id? Also which SDK/version?

jamal_mobile: Request-id: rwd-req-0a3f9b2c. SDK: mobile-js v1.4.2. Client log snippet: 
```
[stream] open id=0
[stream] chunk: {"text":"So far so good..."}
[net] network change -> IKEv2
[stream] error id=0 code=ECONNRESET
```
I can repro 9/10 by toggling VPN midstream.

maria_eng: Do you see any server-side correlation? I pulled the proxy logs for rwd-req-0a3f9b2c — upstream shows connection closed by client after ~42s, no server error. Proxy idle timeout is 35s in front of our streaming pool for connections with no intermediate flushing.

jamal_mobile: Huh, we do stream tokens every ~2s normally. But when the model returns a long initial prefix (no chunks for 30s) then a burst, it looks like the VPN switch kills the TCP 4-tuple and the client socket never sends the FIN.

lisa_support: Quick clarifying question — is the app using the SDK's default keepalive/ping? Mobile client uses WebSocket?

jamal_mobile: It's SSE over a persistent HTTP connection. We rely on default browser/app TCP keepalive. No application-level heartbeat.

maria_eng: Root cause hypothesis: carrier/VPN NAT or OS path-change resets the socket. Because there is a long quiet window (no small chunks), intermediate NAT state or proxy times out the flow. When network changes, Android's socket doesn't always close cleanly, so we get ECONNRESET on reuse.

alex_support: Two immediate mitigations: 
- Client: enable app-level heartbeats (send a minimal comment chunk for SSE or a zero-length event) every 15s while waiting. Example SSE ping: `: keepalive\n\n`
- Server: reduce proxy idle timeout for streams that advertise long-tail behavior, or send periodic flushes if model generation stalls.

maria_eng: Adding code examples — server side (node/express) force flush: 
```js
res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream');
res.write(':init\n\n'); // initial comment
// later, while generating:
setInterval(() => res.write(':hb\n\n'), 15000);
```
Client-side (android okhttp) enable TCP keepalive: 
```
socket.setKeepAlive(true);
// or okhttp ping interval for web sockets
```

jamal_mobile: Trying SSE comment pings now. One more question: is there any token refresh or auth race that could cause mid-stream close? We saw token rotate logs for other threads.

maria_eng: For this request id there was no token rotation. Token refresh can cause intentional 401s mid-stream only if client re-auths and issues new connection without draining old. That doesn't match your ECONNRESET trace.

lisa_support: I've opened a support ticket INC-2026 and flagged infra; adding repro steps + logs. Will follow up. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026 created by lisa_support — priority P2. Link: https://redwood/support/INC-2026

alex_support: Follow-up items: 
- Jamal: add client heartbeat and confirm repro rate drops.
- Maria: evaluate proxy idle timeout or enable server heartbeat for streaming pool.
- Lisa: attach customer-facing workaround and ETA in INC-2026.

jamal_mobile: Will test heartbeat patch and report back in this thread. Thanks.

lisa_support: If heartbeat reduces failure but not eliminates, we'll advise a short-term mobile patch + long-term runtime change (proxy config or server flushes).

jamal_mobile: Update — heartbeat every 12s dropped repro from 9/10 to 1/10 on my test device (Android 11, carrier NAT). Sending full logs to INC-2026.

maria_eng: Great data. We'll schedule a config change in canary to send server-side comment pings for long-running streams and monitor error rate.

alex_support: Marking this thread resolved for now; reopen if you hit the 1/10 case after server canary. :thumbsup:
